transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… my clinic doctor wanted me to come in. She’s been kind of on me about my eating.

I don’t know, I guess I keep it pretty simple most days—coffee in the morning, maybe a few bites of something between jobs, and a small dinner if I’m not too busy with class paperwork.
Have you lost any weight recently?
A little, I guess. My work pants are pretty loose now, and people at job sites keep saying I look too thin. I don’t really see it that way… I’m just on my feet all day, so I figured I’ve leaned out.
Are you worried about gaining weight?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t like to say it like that, but yes. If I eat something heavy—like pizza or a big sandwich—I get really uneasy, like I’m going to wake up bigger and slower. Then I worry I won’t be able to move around ladders or tight rooms the way I need to.
Do you avoid eating certain foods or food groups?

I guess I don’t think of it as avoiding whole food groups exactly. I just… keep things simple. Coffee in the morning, maybe a few bites of something between jobs, and then a small dinner later if I’m not too tied up with class paperwork.
Do you ever feel like you've lost control while eating?
Not really… I don’t think so. I’m usually pretty aware of what I’m eating. I can’t really think of a time where it felt out of control.
Are you trying to control your weight when you limit what you eat?

I… I don’t know if I’d put it that directly. I guess I’m just trying to keep things simple. The clinic doctor got on me about it, but most days it’s coffee, maybe a few bites between jobs, and a small dinner if I’m not too busy with paperwork.
Do you think your eating habits are related to a fear of losing control over your food intake?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think about it like losing control. I just… try to keep things manageable, I guess.
Do you think being thinner would be better for you?

Maybe… I don’t like saying it that way. It’s more that if I eat something heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get this panicky thought that I’ll wake up bigger, slower. And I need to be able to move around ladders and rooms for work, so… yeah, I guess thinner feels safer.
Do you think there's a specific weight or body shape you're trying to achieve?

Not a number, really. I don’t have some exact shape in my head. It’s more… if I eat something heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get scared I’ll wake up bigger and slower. Like I won’t be able to move around ladders and tight rooms the way I need to.
Do you think you would feel better about yourself if you had a different body shape?

Maybe. I don’t know if it’s about “better about myself” exactly. It’s more that when I eat something heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get this panicky feeling that I’ll wake up bigger… slower. And then I think I won’t be able to move around ladders or rooms like I need to.
Do you find that your eating habits are interfering with your daily activities or relationships?

A little, I guess. I’m still getting to jobs and class, so it’s not like I’ve stopped everything. But I’ve been skipping lunches with coworkers, and sometimes study meetups too. It’s just easier to keep things… controlled, I guess, and not have people noticing or saying anything.
Do you ever make yourself vomit or exercise excessively after eating?
No… I don’t make myself throw up. Exercise… I mean, I move a lot for work, but I wouldn’t say it’s like that.
Do you think you would look better if you were thinner?

I don’t know if I’d say “look better.” It’s more… if I eat something heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get scared I’ll wake up bigger. Slower. And then I worry I won’t be able to move around at work the way I need to.
Do you exercise more than what's required for your job?
Not really. I mean, work is already pretty physical, so I don’t usually do extra on purpose.
Do you think gaining a small amount of weight, like a few pounds, would be very upsetting for you?

Yeah… probably. Even a few pounds would make me nervous. I’d start thinking I was going to feel bigger and slower, like after I eat pizza or a big sandwich, and then I worry about getting around ladders and rooms at work.
Are you trying to maintain a certain weight with your current eating habits?

I don’t know if I’d call it trying to maintain a weight exactly. I guess I’m here because the clinic doctor got on me about how I’ve been eating. Most days I just keep it simple… coffee in the morning, maybe a few bites of something between jobs, and then a small dinner if I’m not too busy with class paperwork.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is mostly about how it would affect your ability to work and be physically active?

Yeah… mostly that, I think. Like if I eat something heavy, pizza or a big sandwich, I get this panicky thought that I’ll wake up bigger somehow… slower. And then I start worrying I won’t be able to move around ladders or tight rooms the way I need to.
Do you feel like your eating habits are mainly driven by a desire to perform better physically at work?

Kind of, yeah. It’s not like I’m trying to be better at work exactly… it’s more that if I eat something heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get this panicky feeling I’ll wake up bigger and slower. Then I start worrying about ladders and getting around rooms.
Is your main concern about eating and weight related to how it affects your work performance or how you feel about your body?

I guess it’s both, but I think I tell myself it’s about work. Like… if I eat something heavy, pizza or a big sandwich, I get panicky that I’ll wake up bigger and slower. Then I worry I won’t be able to move around ladders or tight rooms like I need to.
Is your desire to be thinner mostly about how your body looks or about something else?

It’s… not just looks, I don’t think. I mean, I notice that too, but mostly I get scared I’ll feel bigger and slower. Like if I eat pizza or a big sandwich, I start thinking I won’t be able to move around ladders or through rooms the way I need to.
